title: Quickpost: Uranium Glass
content_md: I got the opportunity to measure the radiation emitted by uranium glass . Uranium glass is glass with uranium added to the glass mix for coloration. My Bosean FS-5000 meter did not detect any radiation from the uranium glass. The counts per second (CPS) value was around the same on the uranium glass and away from it. I know it is proper uranium glass (bought at a flea market), because it glows green under ultraviolet light. My meter uses a Geiger–Müller tube , so the tube must not be sensitive enough to detect the radiation from the uranium glass. I also have another meter to measure radiation, a Radiacode 103 meter. It looks like this: It reads out a spot value of 9,57 CPS in the above picture: this is the amount of background radiation in that location, since no radioactive sources were nearby. And here is my Radiacode 103 meter inside a glass made out of uranium glass: The CPS value is 13,5, that’s noticeably higher than the background value of 9,57. Thus the glass is emitting some radiation that this meter is picking up. Strictly speaking, that doesn’t prove it’s uranium glass, because it could be another element that is the source of radiation.
